segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: Okay, thanks for joining. Today I want to walk through the admin-invite onboarding flow, then Hannah will share what we learned from the usability sessions, and then we need to make a few decisions so I can hand this to engineering. I'll share my screen.

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: So this is the first screen after signup. Before, it asked you to paste API credentials straight away. Now there are two big choices: connect it yourself, or invite your admin. Most people who get stuck don't have the credentials, so the second option is highlighted.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Can I ask a quick question? What does the person who clicks invite actually send? Is it an email from us, or from them?

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: It's an email from us, but with their name in the subject and the body, so it reads like a request from a colleague. Something like, Priya is setting up Beacon and needs read-only access to your orders database.

segments.speaker: priya
segments.text: I like that the email says exactly what we access. That was the main fear in the interviews, wasn't it?

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: Yes, that's the thing I'll cover in a minute. Let me let you finish the walkthrough first, then I'll share the data.

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: Right. So, after they send the invite, they land in a sample workspace. It's a fully populated dashboard with demo data, and there's a banner at the top that says, we're waiting for your admin, here's what happens next. And a progress checklist on the right.

segments.speaker: sam
segments.text: And the checklist updates in real time when the admin connects?

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: Yes. The moment credentials are verified, the banner turns into a message, your data is connected, switch to your real workspace, with a single button. We don't switch them automatically, because losing the dashboard they were exploring would be jarring.

segments.speaker: sam
segments.text: Good call.

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: The admin's side is a single page. It shows who asked, what we'll access, how to create a read-only user for the most common databases, and a field to paste the credentials. The link is single use and expires in seventy-two hours.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: Okay, I'll go through the usability results. We ran six sessions last week, all people who recently signed up for a data tool, none of them familiar with Beacon. Five of six found the invite-your-admin option without help, which is great.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: The problem was the words. Four of the six read the phrase read-only access and weren't sure whether it meant we could change their data. Two of them said they'd need to ask their security team before sending it, which is exactly the delay we're trying to avoid.

segments.speaker: priya
segments.text: That's an important finding. So the wording is the risk, not the flow.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: Right. When we replaced read-only access with we can only look at your data, we can never change it, all four said it was clear. So I'm recommending that copy in the email and on the admin page.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: That matches what I hear from prospects. Their IT people want to see the exact permissions, not a reassurance. Could the admin page include the exact SQL grant statement?

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: I can add a copy-to-clipboard block with the grant statement for Postgres, MySQL and the warehouse connectors. That's a small change.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: That would help a lot. Two participants said they would have felt better with that.

segments.speaker: sam
segments.text: What about reminders? If the admin ignores the first email, what happens?

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: I'm proposing a reminder after twenty-four hours and another at seventy-two hours, just before the link expires. After that the signup person gets a nudge to resend it or connect themselves.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: In the sessions, people said one reminder felt helpful and two felt a bit pushy. So maybe the second reminder goes to the person who invited, not to the admin.

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: Oh, that's a good distinction. First reminder to the admin at twenty-four hours. At seventy-two hours the link is about to expire, so we email the person who signed up, not the admin, offering to resend.

segments.speaker: priya
segments.text: On security, I need to flag that legal will want to look at the wording about data access. Can we get sign-off before we ship? I'll take that.

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: Yes please, and the token details too. Single use, seventy-two hours, revocable from the settings page.

segments.speaker: priya
segments.text: I'll bring all of that to them this week.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Now the sample data. For demos, I'd love different industries. Right now it's an e-commerce store, and that doesn't land with a prospect in healthcare or software.

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: For version one I'd do two datasets, e-commerce and a software subscription business, because those are most of our signups. Healthcare and logistics can come later.

segments.speaker: sam
segments.text: Agreed. I looked at our signup survey and those two cover about sixty percent of new workspaces.

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: Okay, I'll write up a spec for the two datasets, what tables and what dashboards each includes, so engineering can build them. I'll have that by the thirteenth.

segments.speaker: sam
segments.text: On measurement, I want to define the funnel events now so we don't retrofit them. Invite sent, invite opened by the admin, credentials submitted, connection verified, first dashboard built. Then we can see exactly where the thirty-one minutes goes.

segments.speaker: priya
segments.text: What's the success metric? I'd like it to be unambiguous.

segments.speaker: sam
segments.text: Median time to first dashboard. It's fifty-two minutes today. The target is under thirty, and I'd like activation at day seven to move from thirty-eight percent toward forty-five.

segments.speaker: priya
segments.text: Good. And how do we roll it out? I don't want to find out we made things worse after everyone has it.

segments.speaker: sam
segments.text: I'd put it behind a flag at fifty percent of new signups, and compare the two groups for three weeks. We get enough signups for that to be meaningful.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Can I get a handful of design partners? I could ask three or four prospects to try it with their IT teams before the public rollout.

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: That would be amazing for feedback. Tom, can you send me three or four contacts who'd be willing?

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Yes, I'll send those by next Thursday.

segments.speaker: priya
segments.text: Let me recap the decisions. We're going with the new copy, we can only look at your data, we can never change it. The admin page includes the grant statements. Reminders at twenty-four hours to the admin, and at seventy-two hours to the person who signed up. Two sample datasets for version one. And we roll it out to half of new signups behind a flag. Did I miss anything?

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: No, that's it. One more open question is whether to offer a Slack option for the invite, in addition to email. Some teams live in Slack.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: Two of my six participants said they'd rather ask in Slack. But it adds a lot of surface area, so I'd say not for version one.

segments.speaker: priya
segments.text: Agreed, not version one. Let's park it as a question for later.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: I'd like to run a second round of tests with the revised copy before we ship. Five sessions, same recruiting. I can have results by Friday the ninth of October.

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: Perfect. I'll update the copy on the credential request page by Friday so you can test it. I'll post the new mocks in the design channel.

segments.speaker: sam
segments.text: And I'll write up the event definitions and a dashboard for the funnel by Monday, so engineering can instrument as they build.

segments.speaker: priya
segments.text: Great, thanks all. This is in much better shape than the first draft.

segments.speaker: elena
segments.text: Thanks everyone. That was really productive.

summary.overview: The team reviewed the admin-invite onboarding flow designed to remove the 31 minutes new users spend waiting for credentials. Usability testing with six people showed five found the invite option unaided, but four misread 'read-only access', so the copy changes to 'we can only look at your data, we can never change it' and the admin page gets copy-paste grant statements. They decided on reminders at 24 hours (to the admin) and 72 hours (to the person who signed up), two sample datasets for version one (e-commerce and software subscription), funnel events for measurement, and a 50% flagged rollout comparing median time to first dashboard against today's 52 minutes.
bullet_points: Flow: signup offers 'connect yourself' or 'invite your admin'; the invitee explores a populated sample workspace with a status banner and live checklist until credentials are verified.
Usability findings: 5 of 6 participants found the invite option; the phrase 'read-only access' confused 4 of 6, and two would have needed security approval first.
Decisions: new copy, copy-to-clipboard SQL grants on the admin page, single-use links that expire in 72 hours, reminders at 24h to the admin and 72h to the inviter, no Slack invite in version one.
Sample data: e-commerce and software subscription datasets for version one (about 60% of signups); healthcare and logistics later.

Measurement: funnel events from invite sent to first dashboard; goal is median time to first dashboard under 30 minutes (from 52) and activation toward 45%, via a 50% flagged rollout over three weeks.

action_items.text: Update the credential request page copy to 'we can only look at your data, we can never change it' and add copy-paste SQL grant blocks
Get legal and security sign-off on the data access wording and token details
Define funnel events and build the admin-invite funnel dashboard
Send three or four prospect contacts willing to pilot the flow with their IT teams
Run a second round of five usability sessions on the revised copy
Write the spec for the e-commerce and software subscription sample datasets
Decide whether a Slack option for invites belongs in a later version
